+\section{Fibonacci prime-power realization}
+\label{sec:prime-power-realization}
+
+The witness-cover classification is structural.  We now supply the
+Fibonacci-specific input that determines which prime powers can occur in its
+atomic families.  These formulas will be used explicitly in the upper bounds.
+
+\begin{proposition}[Classical prime-power rank lifting]
+\label{prop:prime-power-ladders}
+Let $p$ be prime, and put $z_p:=\alpha(p)$. For $p\ne2,5$, put
+$h_p:=\nu_p(F_{z_p})$. Then
+\[
+\alpha(2)=3,\qquad \alpha(4)=6,\qquad
+\alpha(2^e)=3\cdot2^{e-2}\quad(e\ge3),
+\]
+\[
+\alpha(5^e)=5^e\quad(e\ge1),
+\]
+and, for $p\ne2,5$,
+\[
+\alpha(p^e)=p^{\max\{e-h_p,0\}}z_p\quad(e\ge1).
+\]
+\end{proposition}
+
+\begin{proof}
+Wall's rank-divisibility theorem gives
+\[
+p\mid F_r\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad z_p\mid r
+\]
+\cite{Wall1960FibonacciModm}. For $p\ne2,5$, the classical congruence
+\[
+F_{p-(5/p)}\equiv0\pmod p
+\]
+gives $z_p\mid p-(5/p)$, so $p\nmid z_p$. Lengyel's valuation formula
+\cite[Theorems~1 and~2]{Lengyel1995OrderFibonacciLucas}, in the treatment of
+Medina--Rowland \cite{MedinaRowland2015PRegularity}, states that when
+$z_p\mid r$,
+\[
+\nu_p(F_r)=\nu_p(F_{z_p})+\nu_p(r).
+\]
+Writing $r=z_pu$ yields
+$\nu_p(F_{z_pu})=h_p+\nu_p(u)$. Thus $p^e\mid F_{z_pu}$ if and only if
+$\nu_p(u)\ge e-h_p$, and the least admissible $u$ is
+$p^{\max\{e-h_p,0\}}$.
+
+For the exceptional primes, the same valuation formulas specialize to
+\[
+\nu_5(F_r)=\nu_5(r),
+\qquad
+\nu_2(F_r)=
+\begin{cases}
+0, & 3\nmid r,\\
+1, & r\equiv3\pmod 6,\\
+3, & r\equiv6\pmod {12},\\
+\nu_2(r)+2, & 12\mid r.
+\end{cases}
+\]
+The least index divisible by $5^e$ is $5^e$. For $2$, the least indices
+with valuation at least $1$, $2$, and $3$ are $3$, $6$, and $6$; for
+$e\ge4$ the least admissible multiple of $12$ is $3\cdot2^{e-2}$.
+\end{proof}
+
+\begin{corollary}[Atomic prime-power classification]
+\label{cor:atomic-classification}
+The atomic prime powers are exactly the following:
+\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
+\item $2\in\Atom(3)$, $4\in\Atom(6)$, and
+$2^e\in\Atom(3\cdot2^{e-2})$ for every $e\ge4$; the power $8$ is not
+atomic.
+\item $5^e\in\Atom(5^e)$ for every $e\ge1$.
+\item If $p\ne2,5$, $z_p=\alpha(p)$, and
+$h_p=\nu_p(F_{z_p})$, then $p\in\Atom(z_p)$ and
+$p^e\in\Atom(p^{e-h_p}z_p)$ for every $e>h_p$; no power $p^e$ with
+$1<e\le h_p$ is atomic.
+\end{enumerate}
+Consequently every atom is either a prime atom or a ladder atom $p^e$ with
+$e>1$. Every ladder step changes only the $p$-adic coordinate of its
+apparition index when it is lowered to $p^{e-1}$.
+\end{corollary}
+
+\begin{proof}
+Apply Proposition~\ref{prop:prime-power-ladders}. For $p=2$, the ranks are
+$3,6,6,12,24,\ldots$ on $2,4,8,16,32,\ldots$. For $p=5$, every step is
+atomic. If $p\ne2,5$, the rank remains $z_p$ for $1\le e\le h_p$ and then
+gains one factor of $p$ at each further level. The last assertion follows
+from the same formulas.
+\end{proof}
+
+\begin{lemma}[Prime-ladder dichotomy]
+\label{thm:primitive-ladder-dichotomy}
+Let $\theta=p^e\in\Atom(d)$ and suppose $d\mid n$. If $e=1$, then
+\[
+E_n(\theta)=T_n(\theta).
+\]
+If $e>1$, then $E_n(\theta)$ is either empty or the singleton $\{p\}$.
+In particular, no Fibonacci atom has
+\[
+1<\#E_n(\theta)<\#T_n(\theta).
+\]
+\end{lemma}
+
+\begin{proof}
+If $e=1$, then $d^-(\theta)=\alpha(1)=1$, so every coordinate in
+$T_n(\theta)$ is lost after lowering. Assume $e>1$. By
+Corollary~\ref{cor:atomic-classification}, $\theta$ is a ladder atom.
+Proposition~\ref{prop:prime-power-ladders} shows that $d(\theta)$ and
+$d^-(\theta)$ differ only in their $p$-adic coordinate. Therefore the only
+full coordinate that can be lost is $p$ itself, and the result follows.
+\end{proof}
+
+For nonempty $J\subseteq\mathcal P(n)$, define the prime window
+\[
+P_J(n):=\coprod_{\substack{d\mid n\\T_n(d)=J}}\Pi_\alpha(d),
+\]
+where $T_n(d)=\{\ell\in\mathcal P(n):
+\nu_\ell(d)=\nu_\ell(n)\}$.  A prime in $P_J(n)$ is identified with its
+prime atom.
+
+\begin{proposition}[Atomic families and unique ladder slots]
+\label{prop:atomic-family-ladder-slots}
+Let $n\ge3$ and let $\varnothing\ne I\subseteq J\subseteq\mathcal P(n)$.
+Then every atom in $\mathcal A_{I,J}(n)$ is either in the prime window
+$P_J(n)$, which occurs only when $I=J$, or in a ladder family with
+$I=\{p\}$ for a prime coordinate $p\in J$.  Each such ladder family contains
+at most one atom.
+
+More precisely, put $a=\nu_p(n)$.  Its only possible ladder atom is
+\[
+\lambda_p(n)=
+\begin{cases}
+4, & p=2,\ a=1,\\
+2^{a+2}, & p=2,\ a\ge2,\\
+5^a, & p=5,\ a\ge2,\\
+p^{h_p+a}, & p\notin\{2,5\},
+\end{cases}
+\]
+with no candidate for $p=5$, $a=1$.  The candidate belongs to
+$\mathcal A_{\{p\},J}(n)$ exactly when
+$d(\lambda_p(n))\mid n$ and $T_n(\lambda_p(n))=J$.
+Consequently every atomic family is finite, every nonsingleton atomic family
+is a finite disjoint union of exact-rank prime classes, and every labelled
+ladder slot has at most one candidate.
+\end{proposition}
+
+\begin{proof}
+If $\theta=q$ is a prime atom, the prime-ladder dichotomy gives
+$E_n(q)=T_n(q)$, and $q$ belongs to the unique class
+$\Pi_\alpha(d(q))$ in $P_{T_n(q)}(n)$. Conversely every prime in $P_J(n)$
+has $(E_n,T_n)=(J,J)$.
+
+Suppose $\theta=q^e$ is a ladder atom. The same dichotomy gives
+$E_n(\theta)=\{q\}$ whenever the essential support is nonempty. Hence its
+essential coordinate determines its underlying prime, so $q=p$. The
+full-exponent equation
+$\nu_p(d(p^e))=\nu_p(n)=a$ and
+Proposition~\ref{prop:prime-power-ladders} now leave only the displayed
+candidate. For $p=2$, the atomic ladder levels are $4$ of rank $6$ and
+$2^e$ of rank $3\cdot2^{e-2}$ for $e\ge4$. For $p=5$, the rank is $5^e$,
+and $e=1$ is a prime atom. For $p\notin\{2,5\}$, one has
+$p\nmid z_p$ and
+$\alpha(p^e)=p^{e-h_p}z_p$ at atomic ladder levels, so $e=h_p+a$.
+The remaining conditions $d(\theta)\mid n$ and $T_n(\theta)=J$ are exactly
+the conditions for membership in $\mathcal A_{\{p\},J}(n)$.
+
+Finally, each $\Pi_\alpha(d)$ is finite by
+Lemma~\ref{lem:primitive-prime-mobius-count}, and there are only finitely many
+divisors $d$ of $n$. This proves all finiteness and uniqueness assertions.
+\end{proof}

-\begin{theorem}[Fibotomic rank entropy]
+The Fibonacci polynomials were studied by Webb--Parberry
+\cite{WebbParberry1969FibonacciPolynomials}; Levy introduced the fibotomic
+polynomials and proved their irreducibility over $\mathbb Q$
+\cite{Levy2001FibonacciPolynomials}; and Byer--Dvorachek--Eckard--Harrington--
+Wise--Wong developed their later systematic theory
+\cite{CameronCountsLundMillerPiechnikWong2022Fibotomic}. We use only the
+definition and factorization identity recorded in the following lemma.
+
+\begin{lemma}[Fibotomic integer and exact-rank radical]
+\label{lem:fibotomic-integer-radical}
+Let $d\ge3$, let $\Psi_d(x)$ be the $d$th fibotomic polynomial, and put
+\[
+ \mathfrak F_d:=\prod_{r\mid d}F_r^{\mu(d/r)}.
+\]
+Then
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:fibotomic-integer-identity}
+ \mathfrak F_d=\Psi_d(1)\in\mathbb N,
+\end{equation}
+and
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:exact-rank-radical-divides-fibotomic}
+ \prod_{p\in\Pi_\alpha(d)}p\mid\mathfrak F_d.
+\end{equation}
+For $d=3,5$ the exact-rank radicals are respectively $2$ and $5$; for
+$d=6,12$ the exact-rank layer is empty, so the product in the second display
+is $1$.
+\end{lemma}
+
+\begin{proof}
+The polynomial factorization
+\[
+ F_d(x)=\prod_{r\mid d}\Psi_r(x)
+\]
+and M\"obius inversion in the multiplicative group of nonzero rational
+functions give
+\[
+ \Psi_d(x)=\prod_{r\mid d}F_r(x)^{\mu(d/r)}.
+\]
+Evaluation at $x=1$ proves
+$\mathfrak F_d=\Psi_d(1)$. The fibotomic polynomial has positive integral
+value at $1$, proving \eqref{eq:fibotomic-integer-identity} despite the
+negative exponents in the M\"obius expression.
+
+If $p\in\Pi_\alpha(d)$, then $p\mid F_d$ but $p\nmid F_r$ for every proper
+divisor $r$ of $d$. In the integral factorization
+$F_d=\prod_{r\mid d}\Psi_r(1)$, any divisibility
+$p\mid\Psi_r(1)$ with $r<d$ would imply $p\mid F_r$, because
+$\Psi_r(1)\mid F_r$. Hence $p\mid\Psi_d(1)=\mathfrak F_d$. Distinct
+exact-rank primes are coprime, which proves the radical divisibility without
+any appeal to cancellation in the M\"obius quotient. The small-rank claims
+follow from $\alpha(2)=3$, $\alpha(5)=5$, and the absence of exact-rank
+primes at ranks $6$ and $12$.
+\end{proof}
+

-\subsection*{Witness covers}
+\end{proof}

+\begin{proposition}[Wagner comparison and lowered labels]
+\label{prop:wagner-comparison}
+Let $n\ge2$, and let $\Theta=\{p_1,\ldots,p_r\}$ be a set of distinct prime
+atoms with $d_i:=\alpha(p_i)\mid n$. Then $\Theta$ is an $n$-witness cover
+if and only if, after forgetting the order of the tuple
+$(d_1,\ldots,d_r)$,
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:wagner-minimal-multiplicative-cover}
+ \lcmop(d_1,\ldots,d_r)=n,
+ \qquad
+ \lcmop(d_1,\ldots,\widehat{d_i},\ldots,d_r)<n
+ \quad(1\le i\le r).
+\end{equation}
+Thus the prime-atom case is precisely the unordered form of Wagner's minimal
+multiplicative cover condition.
+
+For arbitrary pairwise coprime atoms
+$\Theta=\{\theta_1,\ldots,\theta_r\}$, the witness condition replaces the
+deletion in \eqref{eq:wagner-minimal-multiplicative-cover} by
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:lowered-label-multiplicative-cover}
+ \lcmop\bigl(d(\theta_1),\ldots,d^-(\theta_i),\ldots,
+ d(\theta_r)\bigr)<n
+ \quad(1\le i\le r).
+\end{equation}
+In particular, ladder atoms supply the genuinely additional lowered-label
+case: their label is lowered to $d^-(\theta_i)$ rather than deleted.
+\end{proposition}
+
+\begin{proof}
+For a prime atom $p_i$, one has $d^-(p_i)=\alpha(1)=1$. Hence replacing
+$d_i$ by $d^-(p_i)$ in an lcm is identical to omitting $d_i$. Lemma~
+\ref{thm:minimal-generators} and the coordinate test in Lemma~
+\ref{lem:coordinate-lowering-test} then identify the witness-cover conditions
+with \eqref{eq:wagner-minimal-multiplicative-cover}. Since the labels form a
+minimal cover, no repeated label can occur; forgetting tuple order therefore
+produces the corresponding unordered cover without a multiplicity ambiguity.
+
+For arbitrary atoms, the same two lemmas say exactly that the full apparition
+lcm is $n$ and that lowering each atom produces
+\eqref{eq:lowered-label-multiplicative-cover}. The final assertion is the
+distinction between $d^-(p)=1$ for prime atoms and the nontrivial lower rank
+of a ladder atom.
+\end{proof}
+
+Wagner's condition and its set-theoretic predecessor supply the classical
+cover skeleton. The Fibonacci-specific content below is the arithmetic
+realization of its labels by exact-rank primes, the lowered-label refinement
+forced by prime-power ladders, and the unique correspondence with
+$\mathcal M_n$. The canonical squarefree slice and its exact weighted count
+in Section~\ref{sec:rank-pure} are further arithmetic consequences of that
+realization.

+\section{Fibonacci prime-power realization}
+\label{sec:prime-power-realization}
+
+The witness-cover classification is structural.  We now supply the
+Fibonacci-specific input that determines which prime powers can occur in its
+atomic families.  These formulas will be used explicitly in the upper bounds.
+
+\begin{proposition}[Classical prime-power rank lifting]
+\label{prop:prime-power-ladders}
+Let $p$ be prime, and put $z_p:=\alpha(p)$. For $p\ne2,5$, put
+$h_p:=\nu_p(F_{z_p})$. Then
+\[
+\alpha(2)=3,\qquad \alpha(4)=6,\qquad
+\alpha(2^e)=3\cdot2^{e-2}\quad(e\ge3),
+\]
+\[
+\alpha(5^e)=5^e\quad(e\ge1),
+\]
+and, for $p\ne2,5$,
+\[
+\alpha(p^e)=p^{\max\{e-h_p,0\}}z_p\quad(e\ge1).
+\]
+\end{proposition}
+
+\begin{proof}
+Wall's rank-divisibility theorem gives
+\[
+p\mid F_r\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad z_p\mid r
+\]
+\cite{Wall1960FibonacciModm}. For $p\ne2,5$, the classical congruence
+\[
+F_{p-(5/p)}\equiv0\pmod p
+\]
+gives $z_p\mid p-(5/p)$, so $p\nmid z_p$. Lengyel's valuation formula
+\cite[Theorems~1 and~2]{Lengyel1995OrderFibonacciLucas}, in the treatment of
+Medina--Rowland \cite{MedinaRowland2015PRegularity}, states that when
+$z_p\mid r$,
+\[
+\nu_p(F_r)=\nu_p(F_{z_p})+\nu_p(r).
+\]
+Writing $r=z_pu$ yields
+$\nu_p(F_{z_pu})=h_p+\nu_p(u)$. Thus $p^e\mid F_{z_pu}$ if and only if
+$\nu_p(u)\ge e-h_p$, and the least admissible $u$ is
+$p^{\max\{e-h_p,0\}}$.
+
+For the exceptional primes, the same valuation formulas specialize to
+\[
+\nu_5(F_r)=\nu_5(r),
+\qquad
+\nu_2(F_r)=
+\begin{cases}
+0, & 3\nmid r,\\
+1, & r\equiv3\pmod 6,\\
+3, & r\equiv6\pmod {12},\\
+\nu_2(r)+2, & 12\mid r.
+\end{cases}
+\]
+The least index divisible by $5^e$ is $5^e$. For $2$, the least indices
+with valuation at least $1$, $2$, and $3$ are $3$, $6$, and $6$; for
+$e\ge4$ the least admissible multiple of $12$ is $3\cdot2^{e-2}$.
+\end{proof}
+
+\begin{corollary}[Atomic prime-power classification]
+\label{cor:atomic-classification}
+The atomic prime powers are exactly the following:
+\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
+\item $2\in\Atom(3)$, $4\in\Atom(6)$, and
+$2^e\in\Atom(3\cdot2^{e-2})$ for every $e\ge4$; the power $8$ is not
+atomic.
+\item $5^e\in\Atom(5^e)$ for every $e\ge1$.
+\item If $p\ne2,5$, $z_p=\alpha(p)$, and
+$h_p=\nu_p(F_{z_p})$, then $p\in\Atom(z_p)$ and
+$p^e\in\Atom(p^{e-h_p}z_p)$ for every $e>h_p$; no power $p^e$ with
+$1<e\le h_p$ is atomic.
+\end{enumerate}
+Consequently every atom is either a prime atom or a ladder atom $p^e$ with
+$e>1$. Every ladder step changes only the $p$-adic coordinate of its
+apparition index when it is lowered to $p^{e-1}$.
+\end{corollary}
+
+\begin{proof}
+Apply Proposition~\ref{prop:prime-power-ladders}. For $p=2$, the ranks are
+$3,6,6,12,24,\ldots$ on $2,4,8,16,32,\ldots$. For $p=5$, every step is
+atomic. If $p\ne2,5$, the rank remains $z_p$ for $1\le e\le h_p$ and then
+gains one factor of $p$ at each further level. The last assertion follows
+from the same formulas.
+\end{proof}
+
+\begin{lemma}[Prime-ladder dichotomy]
+\label{thm:primitive-ladder-dichotomy}
+Let $\theta=p^e\in\Atom(d)$ and suppose $d\mid n$. If $e=1$, then
+\[
+E_n(\theta)=T_n(\theta).
+\]
+If $e>1$, then $E_n(\theta)$ is either empty or the singleton $\{p\}$.
+In particular, no Fibonacci atom has
+\[
+1<\#E_n(\theta)<\#T_n(\theta).
+\]
+\end{lemma}
+
+\begin{proof}
+If $e=1$, then $d^-(\theta)=\alpha(1)=1$, so every coordinate in
+$T_n(\theta)$ is lost after lowering. Assume $e>1$. By
+Corollary~\ref{cor:atomic-classification}, $\theta$ is a ladder atom.
+Proposition~\ref{prop:prime-power-ladders} shows that $d(\theta)$ and
+$d^-(\theta)$ differ only in their $p$-adic coordinate. Therefore the only
+full coordinate that can be lost is $p$ itself, and the result follows.
+\end{proof}
+
+For nonempty $J\subseteq\mathcal P(n)$, define the prime window
+\[
+P_J(n):=\coprod_{\substack{d\mid n\\T_n(d)=J}}\Pi_\alpha(d),
+\]
+where $T_n(d)=\{\ell\in\mathcal P(n):
+\nu_\ell(d)=\nu_\ell(n)\}$.  A prime in $P_J(n)$ is identified with its
+prime atom.
+
+\begin{proposition}[Atomic families and unique ladder slots]
+\label{prop:atomic-family-ladder-slots}
+Let $n\ge3$ and let $\varnothing\ne I\subseteq J\subseteq\mathcal P(n)$.
+Then every atom in $\mathcal A_{I,J}(n)$ is either in the prime window
+$P_J(n)$, which occurs only when $I=J$, or in a ladder family with
+$I=\{p\}$ for a prime coordinate $p\in J$.  Each such ladder family contains
+at most one atom.
+
+More precisely, put $a=\nu_p(n)$.  Its only possible ladder atom is
+\[
+\lambda_p(n)=
+\begin{cases}
+4, & p=2,\ a=1,\\
+2^{a+2}, & p=2,\ a\ge2,\\
+5^a, & p=5,\ a\ge2,\\
+p^{h_p+a}, & p\notin\{2,5\},
+\end{cases}
+\]
+with no candidate for $p=5$, $a=1$.  The candidate belongs to
+$\mathcal A_{\{p\},J}(n)$ exactly when
+$d(\lambda_p(n))\mid n$ and $T_n(\lambda_p(n))=J$.
+Consequently every atomic family is finite, every nonsingleton atomic family
+is a finite disjoint union of exact-rank prime classes, and every labelled
+ladder slot has at most one candidate.
+\end{proposition}
+
+\begin{proof}
+If $\theta=q$ is a prime atom, the prime-ladder dichotomy gives
+$E_n(q)=T_n(q)$, and $q$ belongs to the unique class
+$\Pi_\alpha(d(q))$ in $P_{T_n(q)}(n)$. Conversely every prime in $P_J(n)$
+has $(E_n,T_n)=(J,J)$.
+
+Suppose $\theta=q^e$ is a ladder atom. The same dichotomy gives
+$E_n(\theta)=\{q\}$ whenever the essential support is nonempty. Hence its
+essential coordinate determines its underlying prime, so $q=p$. The
+full-exponent equation
+$\nu_p(d(p^e))=\nu_p(n)=a$ and
+Proposition~\ref{prop:prime-power-ladders} now leave only the displayed
+candidate. For $p=2$, the atomic ladder levels are $4$ of rank $6$ and
+$2^e$ of rank $3\cdot2^{e-2}$ for $e\ge4$. For $p=5$, the rank is $5^e$,
+and $e=1$ is a prime atom. For $p\notin\{2,5\}$, one has
+$p\nmid z_p$ and
+$\alpha(p^e)=p^{e-h_p}z_p$ at atomic ladder levels, so $e=h_p+a$.
+The remaining conditions $d(\theta)\mid n$ and $T_n(\theta)=J$ are exactly
+the conditions for membership in $\mathcal A_{\{p\},J}(n)$.
+
+Finally, each $\Pi_\alpha(d)$ is finite by
+Lemma~\ref{lem:primitive-prime-mobius-count}, and there are only finitely many
+divisors $d$ of $n$. This proves all finiteness and uniqueness assertions.
+\end{proof}

-\begin{theorem}[Fibotomic rank entropy]
+The Fibonacci polynomials were studied by Webb--Parberry
+\cite{WebbParberry1969FibonacciPolynomials}; Levy introduced the fibotomic
+polynomials and proved their irreducibility over $\mathbb Q$
+\cite{Levy2001FibonacciPolynomials}; and Byer--Dvorachek--Eckard--Harrington--
+Wise--Wong developed their later systematic theory
+\cite{CameronCountsLundMillerPiechnikWong2022Fibotomic}. We use only the
+definition and factorization identity recorded in the following lemma.
+
+\begin{lemma}[Fibotomic integer and exact-rank radical]
+\label{lem:fibotomic-integer-radical}
+Let $d\ge3$, let $\Psi_d(x)$ be the $d$th fibotomic polynomial, and put
+\[
+ \mathfrak F_d:=\prod_{r\mid d}F_r^{\mu(d/r)}.
+\]
+Then
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:fibotomic-integer-identity}
+ \mathfrak F_d=\Psi_d(1)\in\mathbb N,
+\end{equation}
+and
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:exact-rank-radical-divides-fibotomic}
+ \prod_{p\in\Pi_\alpha(d)}p\mid\mathfrak F_d.
+\end{equation}
+For $d=3,5$ the exact-rank radicals are respectively $2$ and $5$; for
+$d=6,12$ the exact-rank layer is empty, so the product in the second display
+is $1$.
+\end{lemma}
+
+\begin{proof}
+The polynomial factorization
+\[
+ F_d(x)=\prod_{r\mid d}\Psi_r(x)
+\]
+and M\"obius inversion in the multiplicative group of nonzero rational
+functions give
+\[
+ \Psi_d(x)=\prod_{r\mid d}F_r(x)^{\mu(d/r)}.
+\]
+Evaluation at $x=1$ proves
+$\mathfrak F_d=\Psi_d(1)$. The fibotomic polynomial has positive integral
+value at $1$, proving \eqref{eq:fibotomic-integer-identity} despite the
+negative exponents in the M\"obius expression.
+
+If $p\in\Pi_\alpha(d)$, then $p\mid F_d$ but $p\nmid F_r$ for every proper
+divisor $r$ of $d$. In the integral factorization
+$F_d=\prod_{r\mid d}\Psi_r(1)$, any divisibility
+$p\mid\Psi_r(1)$ with $r<d$ would imply $p\mid F_r$, because
+$\Psi_r(1)\mid F_r$. Hence $p\mid\Psi_d(1)=\mathfrak F_d$. Distinct
+exact-rank primes are coprime, which proves the radical divisibility without
+any appeal to cancellation in the M\"obius quotient. The small-rank claims
+follow from $\alpha(2)=3$, $\alpha(5)=5$, and the absence of exact-rank
+primes at ranks $6$ and $12$.
+\end{proof}
+

+\begin{proposition}[Wagner comparison and lowered labels]
+\label{prop:wagner-comparison}
+Let $n\ge2$, and let $\Theta=\{p_1,\ldots,p_r\}$ be a set of distinct prime
+atoms with $d_i:=\alpha(p_i)\mid n$. Then $\Theta$ is an $n$-witness cover
+if and only if, after forgetting the order of the tuple
+$(d_1,\ldots,d_r)$,
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:wagner-minimal-multiplicative-cover}
+ \lcmop(d_1,\ldots,d_r)=n,
+ \qquad
+ \lcmop(d_1,\ldots,\widehat{d_i},\ldots,d_r)<n
+ \quad(1\le i\le r).
+\end{equation}
+Thus the prime-atom case is precisely the unordered form of Wagner's minimal
+multiplicative cover condition.
+
+For arbitrary pairwise coprime atoms
+$\Theta=\{\theta_1,\ldots,\theta_r\}$, the witness condition replaces the
+deletion in \eqref{eq:wagner-minimal-multiplicative-cover} by
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:lowered-label-multiplicative-cover}
+ \lcmop\bigl(d(\theta_1),\ldots,d^-(\theta_i),\ldots,
+ d(\theta_r)\bigr)<n
+ \quad(1\le i\le r).
+\end{equation}
+In particular, ladder atoms supply the genuinely additional lowered-label
+case: their label is lowered to $d^-(\theta_i)$ rather than deleted.
+\end{proposition}
+
+\begin{proof}
+For a prime atom $p_i$, one has $d^-(p_i)=\alpha(1)=1$. Hence replacing
+$d_i$ by $d^-(p_i)$ in an lcm is identical to omitting $d_i$. Lemma~
+\ref{thm:minimal-generators} and the coordinate test in Lemma~
+\ref{lem:coordinate-lowering-test} then identify the witness-cover conditions
+with \eqref{eq:wagner-minimal-multiplicative-cover}. Since the labels form a
+minimal cover, no repeated label can occur; forgetting tuple order therefore
+produces the corresponding unordered cover without a multiplicity ambiguity.
+
+For arbitrary atoms, the same two lemmas say exactly that the full apparition
+lcm is $n$ and that lowering each atom produces
+\eqref{eq:lowered-label-multiplicative-cover}. The final assertion is the
+distinction between $d^-(p)=1$ for prime atoms and the nontrivial lower rank
+of a ladder atom.
+\end{proof}
+
+Wagner's condition and its set-theoretic predecessor supply the classical
+cover skeleton. The Fibonacci-specific content below is the arithmetic
+realization of its labels by exact-rank primes, the lowered-label refinement
+forced by prime-power ladders, and the unique correspondence with
+$\mathcal M_n$. The canonical squarefree slice and its exact weighted count
+in Section~\ref{sec:rank-pure} are further arithmetic consequences of that
+realization.

+\section{Fibonacci prime-power realization}
+\label{sec:prime-power-realization}
+
+The witness-cover classification is structural.  We now supply the
+Fibonacci-specific input that determines which prime powers can occur in its
+atomic families.  These formulas will be used explicitly in the upper bounds.
+
+\begin{proposition}[Classical prime-power rank lifting]
+\label{prop:prime-power-ladders}
+Let $p$ be prime, and put $z_p:=\alpha(p)$. For $p\ne2,5$, put
+$h_p:=\nu_p(F_{z_p})$. Then
+\[
+\alpha(2)=3,\qquad \alpha(4)=6,\qquad
+\alpha(2^e)=3\cdot2^{e-2}\quad(e\ge3),
+\]
+\[
+\alpha(5^e)=5^e\quad(e\ge1),
+\]
+and, for $p\ne2,5$,
+\[
+\alpha(p^e)=p^{\max\{e-h_p,0\}}z_p\quad(e\ge1).
+\]
+\end{proposition}
+
+\begin{proof}
+Wall's rank-divisibility theorem gives
+\[
+p\mid F_r\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad z_p\mid r
+\]
+\cite{Wall1960FibonacciModm}. For $p\ne2,5$, the classical congruence
+\[
+F_{p-(5/p)}\equiv0\pmod p
+\]
+gives $z_p\mid p-(5/p)$, so $p\nmid z_p$. Lengyel's valuation formula
+\cite[Theorems~1 and~2]{Lengyel1995OrderFibonacciLucas}, in the treatment of
+Medina--Rowland \cite{MedinaRowland2015PRegularity}, states that when
+$z_p\mid r$,
+\[
+\nu_p(F_r)=\nu_p(F_{z_p})+\nu_p(r).
+\]
+Writing $r=z_pu$ yields
+$\nu_p(F_{z_pu})=h_p+\nu_p(u)$. Thus $p^e\mid F_{z_pu}$ if and only if
+$\nu_p(u)\ge e-h_p$, and the least admissible $u$ is
+$p^{\max\{e-h_p,0\}}$.
+
+For the exceptional primes, the same valuation formulas specialize to
+\[
+\nu_5(F_r)=\nu_5(r),
+\qquad
+\nu_2(F_r)=
+\begin{cases}
+0, & 3\nmid r,\\
+1, & r\equiv3\pmod 6,\\
+3, & r\equiv6\pmod {12},\\
+\nu_2(r)+2, & 12\mid r.
+\end{cases}
+\]
+The least index divisible by $5^e$ is $5^e$. For $2$, the least indices
+with valuation at least $1$, $2$, and $3$ are $3$, $6$, and $6$; for
+$e\ge4$ the least admissible multiple of $12$ is $3\cdot2^{e-2}$.
+\end{proof}
+
+\begin{corollary}[Atomic prime-power classification]
+\label{cor:atomic-classification}
+The atomic prime powers are exactly the following:
+\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
+\item $2\in\Atom(3)$, $4\in\Atom(6)$, and
+$2^e\in\Atom(3\cdot2^{e-2})$ for every $e\ge4$; the power $8$ is not
+atomic.
+\item $5^e\in\Atom(5^e)$ for every $e\ge1$.
+\item If $p\ne2,5$, $z_p=\alpha(p)$, and
+$h_p=\nu_p(F_{z_p})$, then $p\in\Atom(z_p)$ and
+$p^e\in\Atom(p^{e-h_p}z_p)$ for every $e>h_p$; no power $p^e$ with
+$1<e\le h_p$ is atomic.
+\end{enumerate}
+Consequently every atom is either a prime atom or a ladder atom $p^e$ with
+$e>1$. Every ladder step changes only the $p$-adic coordinate of its
+apparition index when it is lowered to $p^{e-1}$.
+\end{corollary}
+
+\begin{proof}
+Apply Proposition~\ref{prop:prime-power-ladders}. For $p=2$, the ranks are
+$3,6,6,12,24,\ldots$ on $2,4,8,16,32,\ldots$. For $p=5$, every step is
+atomic. If $p\ne2,5$, the rank remains $z_p$ for $1\le e\le h_p$ and then
+gains one factor of $p$ at each further level. The last assertion follows
+from the same formulas.
+\end{proof}
+
+\begin{lemma}[Prime-ladder dichotomy]
+\label{thm:primitive-ladder-dichotomy}
+Let $\theta=p^e\in\Atom(d)$ and suppose $d\mid n$. If $e=1$, then
+\[
+E_n(\theta)=T_n(\theta).
+\]
+If $e>1$, then $E_n(\theta)$ is either empty or the singleton $\{p\}$.
+In particular, no Fibonacci atom has
+\[
+1<\#E_n(\theta)<\#T_n(\theta).
+\]
+\end{lemma}
+
+\begin{proof}
+If $e=1$, then $d^-(\theta)=\alpha(1)=1$, so every coordinate in
+$T_n(\theta)$ is lost after lowering. Assume $e>1$. By
+Corollary~\ref{cor:atomic-classification}, $\theta$ is a ladder atom.
+Proposition~\ref{prop:prime-power-ladders} shows that $d(\theta)$ and
+$d^-(\theta)$ differ only in their $p$-adic coordinate. Therefore the only
+full coordinate that can be lost is $p$ itself, and the result follows.
+\end{proof}
+
+For nonempty $J\subseteq\mathcal P(n)$, define the prime window
+\[
+P_J(n):=\coprod_{\substack{d\mid n\\T_n(d)=J}}\Pi_\alpha(d),
+\]
+where $T_n(d)=\{\ell\in\mathcal P(n):
+\nu_\ell(d)=\nu_\ell(n)\}$.  A prime in $P_J(n)$ is identified with its
+prime atom.
+
+\begin{proposition}[Atomic families and unique ladder slots]
+\label{prop:atomic-family-ladder-slots}
+Let $n\ge3$ and let $\varnothing\ne I\subseteq J\subseteq\mathcal P(n)$.
+Then every atom in $\mathcal A_{I,J}(n)$ is either in the prime window
+$P_J(n)$, which occurs only when $I=J$, or in a ladder family with
+$I=\{p\}$ for a prime coordinate $p\in J$.  Each such ladder family contains
+at most one atom.
+
+More precisely, put $a=\nu_p(n)$.  Its only possible ladder atom is
+\[
+\lambda_p(n)=
+\begin{cases}
+4, & p=2,\ a=1,\\
+2^{a+2}, & p=2,\ a\ge2,\\
+5^a, & p=5,\ a\ge2,\\
+p^{h_p+a}, & p\notin\{2,5\},
+\end{cases}
+\]
+with no candidate for $p=5$, $a=1$.  The candidate belongs to
+$\mathcal A_{\{p\},J}(n)$ exactly when
+$d(\lambda_p(n))\mid n$ and $T_n(\lambda_p(n))=J$.
+Consequently every atomic family is finite, every nonsingleton atomic family
+is a finite disjoint union of exact-rank prime classes, and every labelled
+ladder slot has at most one candidate.
+\end{proposition}
+
+\begin{proof}
+If $\theta=q$ is a prime atom, the prime-ladder dichotomy gives
+$E_n(q)=T_n(q)$, and $q$ belongs to the unique class
+$\Pi_\alpha(d(q))$ in $P_{T_n(q)}(n)$. Conversely every prime in $P_J(n)$
+has $(E_n,T_n)=(J,J)$.
+
+Suppose $\theta=q^e$ is a ladder atom. The same dichotomy gives
+$E_n(\theta)=\{q\}$ whenever the essential support is nonempty. Hence its
+essential coordinate determines its underlying prime, so $q=p$. The
+full-exponent equation
+$\nu_p(d(p^e))=\nu_p(n)=a$ and
+Proposition~\ref{prop:prime-power-ladders} now leave only the displayed
+candidate. For $p=2$, the atomic ladder levels are $4$ of rank $6$ and
+$2^e$ of rank $3\cdot2^{e-2}$ for $e\ge4$. For $p=5$, the rank is $5^e$,
+and $e=1$ is a prime atom. For $p\notin\{2,5\}$, one has
+$p\nmid z_p$ and
+$\alpha(p^e)=p^{e-h_p}z_p$ at atomic ladder levels, so $e=h_p+a$.
+The remaining conditions $d(\theta)\mid n$ and $T_n(\theta)=J$ are exactly
+the conditions for membership in $\mathcal A_{\{p\},J}(n)$.
+
+Finally, each $\Pi_\alpha(d)$ is finite by
+Lemma~\ref{lem:primitive-prime-mobius-count}, and there are only finitely many
+divisors $d$ of $n$. This proves all finiteness and uniqueness assertions.
+\end{proof}

+\begin{lemma}[Fibotomic integer and exact-rank radical]
+\label{lem:fibotomic-integer-radical}
+Let $d\ge3$, let $\Psi_d(x)$ be the $d$th fibotomic polynomial, and put
+\[
+ \mathfrak F_d:=\prod_{r\mid d}F_r^{\mu(d/r)}.
+\]

+ \mathfrak F_d=\Psi_d(1)\in\mathbb N,
+\end{equation}

+\begin{equation}\label{eq:exact-rank-radical-divides-fibotomic}
+ \prod_{p\in\Pi_\alpha(d)}p\mid\mathfrak F_d.
+\end{equation}
+For $d=3,5$ the exact-rank radicals are respectively $2$ and $5$; for
+$d=6,12$ the exact-rank layer is empty, so the product in the second display
+is $1$.
+\end{lemma}

+\begin{proof}
+The polynomial factorization
+\[
+ F_d(x)=\prod_{r\mid d}\Psi_r(x)
+\]
+and M\"obius inversion in the multiplicative group of nonzero rational
+functions give
+\[
+ \Psi_d(x)=\prod_{r\mid d}F_r(x)^{\mu(d/r)}.
+\]
+Evaluation at $x=1$ proves
+$\mathfrak F_d=\Psi_d(1)$. The fibotomic polynomial has positive integral
+value at $1$, proving \eqref{eq:fibotomic-integer-identity} despite the
+negative exponents in the M\"obius expression.
+

+any appeal to cancellation in the M\"obius quotient. The small-rank claims
+follow from $\alpha(2)=3$, $\alpha(5)=5$, and the absence of exact-rank

+\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[Wagner comparison and lowered labels]
\label{prop:wagner-comparison}
Let $n\ge2$, and let $\Theta=\{p_1,\ldots,p_r\}$ be a set of distinct prime
atoms with $d_i:=\alpha(p_i)\mid n$. Then $\Theta$ is an $n$-witness cover
if and only if, after forgetting the order of the tuple
$(d_1,\ldots,d_r)$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:wagner-minimal-multiplicative-cover}
 \lcmop(d_1,\ldots,d_r)=n,
 \qquad
 \lcmop(d_1,\ldots,\widehat{d_i},\ldots,d_r)<n
 \quad(1\le i\le r).
\end{equation}
Thus the prime-atom case is precisely the unordered form of Wagner's minimal
multiplicative cover condition.

For arbitrary pairwise coprime atoms
$\Theta=\{\theta_1,\ldots,\theta_r\}$, the witness condition replaces the
deletion in \eqref{eq:wagner-minimal-multiplicative-cover} by
\begin{equation}\label{eq:lowered-label-multiplicative-cover}
 \lcmop\bigl(d(\theta_1),\ldots,d^-(\theta_i),\ldots,
 d(\theta_r)\bigr)<n
 \quad(1\le i\le r).
\end{equation}
In particular, ladder atoms supply the genuinely additional lowered-label
case: their label is lowered to $d^-(\theta_i)$ rather than deleted.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
For a prime atom $p_i$, one has $d^-(p_i)=\alpha(1)=1$. Hence replacing
$d_i$ by $d^-(p_i)$ in an lcm is identical to omitting $d_i$. Lemma~
\ref{thm:minimal-generators} and the coordinate test in Lemma~
\ref{lem:coordinate-lowering-test} then identify the witness-cover conditions
with \eqref{eq:wagner-minimal-multiplicative-cover}. Since the labels form a
minimal cover, no repeated label can occur; forgetting tuple order therefore
produces the corresponding unordered cover without a multiplicity ambiguity.

For arbitrary atoms, the same two lemmas say exactly that the full apparition
lcm is $n$ and that lowering each atom produces
\eqref{eq:lowered-label-multiplicative-cover}. The final assertion is the
distinction between $d^-(p)=1$ for prime atoms and the nontrivial lower rank
of a ladder atom.
\end{proof}

Wagner's condition and its set-theoretic predecessor supply the classical
cover skeleton. The Fibonacci-specific content below is the arithmetic
realization of its labels by exact-rank primes, the lowered-label refinement
forced by prime-power ladders, and the unique correspondence with
$\mathcal M_n$. The canonical squarefree slice and its exact weighted count
in Section~\ref{sec:rank-pure} are further arithmetic consequences of that
realization.

\subsection*{Witness covers}

\begin{definition}\label{def:witness-cover}
An \emph{$n$-witness cover} is a finite set
$\Theta=\{\theta_1,\ldots,\theta_r\}$ of atomic prime powers satisfying:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
\item $d(\theta)\mid n$ for every $\theta\in\Theta$;
\item the elements of $\Theta$ are pairwise coprime;
\item the full-coordinate supports cover all prime coordinates of $n$,
\[
\bigcup_{\theta\in\Theta}T_n(\theta)=\mathcal P(n);
\]
\item each atom has an essential coordinate not supplied by the other atoms,
\[
E_n(\theta)\nsubseteq
\bigcup_{\eta\in\Theta,\ \eta\ne\theta}T_n(\eta)
\qquad(\theta\in\Theta).
\]
\end{enumerate}
The last condition is the irredundance condition. It is stated with
$E_n$ rather than $T_n$ because overlapping full-coordinate support is
allowed; what is forbidden is that every coordinate lost by lowering
$\theta$ is already supplied at full exponent by the remaining atoms.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Coordinate test for lowering one atom]
\label{lem:coordinate-lowering-test}
Let $n\ge2$, and let
$\Theta=\{\theta_1,\ldots,\theta_r\}$ be a pairwise coprime set of atomic
prime powers with $d(\theta_i)\mid n$ and
\[
\lcmop(d(\theta_1),\ldots,d(\theta_r))=n.
\]
Fix $\theta_i=p_i^{e_i}$, and put
\[
N_i^-:=\lcmop\bigl(d^-(\theta_i),\ d(\theta_j):j\ne i\bigr).
\]
Then $N_i^-=n$ if and only if
\[
E_n(\theta_i)\subseteq\bigcup_{j\ne i}T_n(\theta_j).
\]
Equivalently, lowering $\theta_i$ to $p_i^{e_i-1}$ keeps the apparition lcm
equal to $n$ exactly when every coordinate lost by the lowering is supplied at
full exponent by some other atom. If
$\ell\in E_n(\theta_i)\setminus\bigcup_{j\ne i}T_n(\theta_j)$, then
$\nu_\ell(N_i^-)<\nu_\ell(n)$, so $N_i^-<n$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
Since $d^-(\theta_i)\mid d(\theta_i)\mid n$ and $d(\theta_j)\mid n$ for
$j\ne i$, the integer $N_i^-$ divides $n$. Hence $N_i^-=n$ is equivalent to
saying that every prime coordinate $\ell\in\mathcal P(n)$ occurs in $N_i^-$
with valuation $\nu_\ell(n)$.

Assume first that
$E_n(\theta_i)\subseteq\bigcup_{j\ne i}T_n(\theta_j)$, and fix
$\ell\in\mathcal P(n)$. Because the original lcm is $n$, at least one of the
numbers $d(\theta_1),\ldots,d(\theta_r)$ supplies the full
$\ell$-adic valuation of $n$. If such a supplier is some $d(\theta_j)$ with
$j\ne i$, then $\ell\in T_n(\theta_j)$ and the same full valuation appears in
$N_i^-$. The only remaining case is that $\theta_i$ itself supplies the full
valuation and no other atom does, so $\ell\in T_n(\theta_i)$ and
$\ell\notin\bigcup_{j\ne i}T_n(\theta_j)$. The assumed containment then gives
$\ell\notin E_n(\theta_i)$. By the definition of $E_n(\theta_i)$,
$\nu_\ell(d^-(\theta_i))=\nu_\ell(n)$, so the lowered factor still supplies the
full $\ell$-coordinate in $N_i^-$. Thus every coordinate of $n$ is still
present at full valuation, and $N_i^-=n$.

Conversely, suppose that some coordinate
$\ell\in E_n(\theta_i)$ is not in $\bigcup_{j\ne i}T_n(\theta_j)$. The
membership $\ell\in E_n(\theta_i)$ says
$\nu_\ell(d^-(\theta_i))<\nu_\ell(n)$. For every $j\ne i$, the exclusion
$\ell\notin T_n(\theta_j)$ says
$\nu_\ell(d(\theta_j))<\nu_\ell(n)$. Therefore the lcm defining $N_i^-$ also
has $\ell$-adic valuation strictly below $\nu_\ell(n)$. Since $N_i^-\mid n$,
this proves $N_i^-<n$.
\end{proof}

For every $n\ge 2$, multiplication gives a bijection

+\end{proof}

+\begin{proposition}[Wagner comparison and lowered labels]
+\label{prop:wagner-comparison}
+Let $n\ge2$, and let $\Theta=\{p_1,\ldots,p_r\}$ be a set of distinct prime
+atoms with $d_i:=\alpha(p_i)\mid n$. Then $\Theta$ is an $n$-witness cover
+if and only if, after forgetting the order of the tuple
+$(d_1,\ldots,d_r)$,
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:wagner-minimal-multiplicative-cover}
+ \lcmop(d_1,\ldots,d_r)=n,
+ \qquad
+ \lcmop(d_1,\ldots,\widehat{d_i},\ldots,d_r)<n
+ \quad(1\le i\le r).
+\end{equation}
+Thus the prime-atom case is precisely the unordered form of Wagner's minimal
+multiplicative cover condition.
+
+For arbitrary pairwise coprime atoms
+$\Theta=\{\theta_1,\ldots,\theta_r\}$, the witness condition replaces the
+deletion in \eqref{eq:wagner-minimal-multiplicative-cover} by
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:lowered-label-multiplicative-cover}
+ \lcmop\bigl(d(\theta_1),\ldots,d^-(\theta_i),\ldots,
+ d(\theta_r)\bigr)<n
+ \quad(1\le i\le r).
+\end{equation}
+In particular, ladder atoms supply the genuinely additional lowered-label
+case: their label is lowered to $d^-(\theta_i)$ rather than deleted.
+\end{proposition}
+
+\begin{proof}
+For a prime atom $p_i$, one has $d^-(p_i)=\alpha(1)=1$. Hence replacing
+$d_i$ by $d^-(p_i)$ in an lcm is identical to omitting $d_i$. Lemma~
+\ref{thm:minimal-generators} and the coordinate test in Lemma~
+\ref{lem:coordinate-lowering-test} then identify the witness-cover conditions
+with \eqref{eq:wagner-minimal-multiplicative-cover}. Since the labels form a
+minimal cover, no repeated label can occur; forgetting tuple order therefore
+produces the corresponding unordered cover without a multiplicity ambiguity.
+
+For arbitrary atoms, the same two lemmas say exactly that the full apparition
+lcm is $n$ and that lowering each atom produces
+\eqref{eq:lowered-label-multiplicative-cover}. The final assertion is the
+distinction between $d^-(p)=1$ for prime atoms and the nontrivial lower rank
+of a ladder atom.
+\end{proof}
+
+Wagner's condition and its set-theoretic predecessor supply the classical
+cover skeleton. The Fibonacci-specific content below is the arithmetic
+realization of its labels by exact-rank primes, the lowered-label refinement
+forced by prime-power ladders, and the unique correspondence with
+$\mathcal M_n$. The canonical squarefree slice and its exact weighted count
+in Section~\ref{sec:rank-pure} are further arithmetic consequences of that
+realization.

+\section{Fibonacci prime-power realization}
+\label{sec:prime-power-realization}
+
+The witness-cover classification is structural.  We now supply the
+Fibonacci-specific input that determines which prime powers can occur in its
+atomic families.  These formulas will be used explicitly in the upper bounds.
+
+\begin{proposition}[Classical prime-power rank lifting]
+\label{prop:prime-power-ladders}
+Let $p$ be prime, and put $z_p:=\alpha(p)$. For $p\ne2,5$, put
+$h_p:=\nu_p(F_{z_p})$. Then
+\[
+\alpha(2)=3,\qquad \alpha(4)=6,\qquad
+\alpha(2^e)=3\cdot2^{e-2}\quad(e\ge3),
+\]
+\[
+\alpha(5^e)=5^e\quad(e\ge1),
+\]
+and, for $p\ne2,5$,
+\[
+\alpha(p^e)=p^{\max\{e-h_p,0\}}z_p\quad(e\ge1).
+\]
+\end{proposition}
+
+\begin{proof}
+Wall's rank-divisibility theorem gives
+\[
+p\mid F_r\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad z_p\mid r
+\]
+\cite{Wall1960FibonacciModm}. For $p\ne2,5$, the classical congruence
+\[
+F_{p-(5/p)}\equiv0\pmod p
+\]
+gives $z_p\mid p-(5/p)$, so $p\nmid z_p$. Lengyel's valuation formula
+\cite[Theorems~1 and~2]{Lengyel1995OrderFibonacciLucas}, in the treatment of
+Medina--Rowland \cite{MedinaRowland2015PRegularity}, states that when
+$z_p\mid r$,
+\[
+\nu_p(F_r)=\nu_p(F_{z_p})+\nu_p(r).
+\]
+Writing $r=z_pu$ yields
+$\nu_p(F_{z_pu})=h_p+\nu_p(u)$. Thus $p^e\mid F_{z_pu}$ if and only if
+$\nu_p(u)\ge e-h_p$, and the least admissible $u$ is
+$p^{\max\{e-h_p,0\}}$.
+
+For the exceptional primes, the same valuation formulas specialize to
+\[
+\nu_5(F_r)=\nu_5(r),
+\qquad
+\nu_2(F_r)=
+\begin{cases}
+0, & 3\nmid r,\\
+1, & r\equiv3\pmod 6,\\
+3, & r\equiv6\pmod {12},\\
+\nu_2(r)+2, & 12\mid r.
+\end{cases}
+\]
+The least index divisible by $5^e$ is $5^e$. For $2$, the least indices
+with valuation at least $1$, $2$, and $3$ are $3$, $6$, and $6$; for
+$e\ge4$ the least admissible multiple of $12$ is $3\cdot2^{e-2}$.
+\end{proof}
+
+\begin{corollary}[Atomic prime-power classification]
+\label{cor:atomic-classification}
+The atomic prime powers are exactly the following:
+\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
+\item $2\in\Atom(3)$, $4\in\Atom(6)$, and
+$2^e\in\Atom(3\cdot2^{e-2})$ for every $e\ge4$; the power $8$ is not
+atomic.
+\item $5^e\in\Atom(5^e)$ for every $e\ge1$.
+\item If $p\ne2,5$, $z_p=\alpha(p)$, and
+$h_p=\nu_p(F_{z_p})$, then $p\in\Atom(z_p)$ and
+$p^e\in\Atom(p^{e-h_p}z_p)$ for every $e>h_p$; no power $p^e$ with
+$1<e\le h_p$ is atomic.
+\end{enumerate}
+Consequently every atom is either a prime atom or a ladder atom $p^e$ with
+$e>1$. Every ladder step changes only the $p$-adic coordinate of its
+apparition index when it is lowered to $p^{e-1}$.
+\end{corollary}
+
+\begin{proof}
+Apply Proposition~\ref{prop:prime-power-ladders}. For $p=2$, the ranks are
+$3,6,6,12,24,\ldots$ on $2,4,8,16,32,\ldots$. For $p=5$, every step is
+atomic. If $p\ne2,5$, the rank remains $z_p$ for $1\le e\le h_p$ and then
+gains one factor of $p$ at each further level. The last assertion follows
+from the same formulas.
+\end{proof}
+
+\begin{lemma}[Prime-ladder dichotomy]
+\label{thm:primitive-ladder-dichotomy}
+Let $\theta=p^e\in\Atom(d)$ and suppose $d\mid n$. If $e=1$, then
+\[
+E_n(\theta)=T_n(\theta).
+\]
+If $e>1$, then $E_n(\theta)$ is either empty or the singleton $\{p\}$.
+In particular, no Fibonacci atom has
+\[
+1<\#E_n(\theta)<\#T_n(\theta).
+\]
+\end{lemma}
+
+\begin{proof}
+If $e=1$, then $d^-(\theta)=\alpha(1)=1$, so every coordinate in
+$T_n(\theta)$ is lost after lowering. Assume $e>1$. By
+Corollary~\ref{cor:atomic-classification}, $\theta$ is a ladder atom.
+Proposition~\ref{prop:prime-power-ladders} shows that $d(\theta)$ and
+$d^-(\theta)$ differ only in their $p$-adic coordinate. Therefore the only
+full coordinate that can be lost is $p$ itself, and the result follows.
+\end{proof}
+
+For nonempty $J\subseteq\mathcal P(n)$, define the prime window
+\[
+P_J(n):=\coprod_{\substack{d\mid n\\T_n(d)=J}}\Pi_\alpha(d),
+\]
+where $T_n(d)=\{\ell\in\mathcal P(n):
+\nu_\ell(d)=\nu_\ell(n)\}$.  A prime in $P_J(n)$ is identified with its
+prime atom.
+
+\begin{proposition}[Atomic families and unique ladder slots]
+\label{prop:atomic-family-ladder-slots}
+Let $n\ge3$ and let $\varnothing\ne I\subseteq J\subseteq\mathcal P(n)$.
+Then every atom in $\mathcal A_{I,J}(n)$ is either in the prime window
+$P_J(n)$, which occurs only when $I=J$, or in a ladder family with
+$I=\{p\}$ for a prime coordinate $p\in J$.  Each such ladder family contains
+at most one atom.
+
+More precisely, put $a=\nu_p(n)$.  Its only possible ladder atom is
+\[
+\lambda_p(n)=
+\begin{cases}
+4, & p=2,\ a=1,\\
+2^{a+2}, & p=2,\ a\ge2,\\
+5^a, & p=5,\ a\ge2,\\
+p^{h_p+a}, & p\notin\{2,5\},
+\end{cases}
+\]
+with no candidate for $p=5$, $a=1$.  The candidate belongs to
+$\mathcal A_{\{p\},J}(n)$ exactly when
+$d(\lambda_p(n))\mid n$ and $T_n(\lambda_p(n))=J$.
+Consequently every atomic family is finite, every nonsingleton atomic family
+is a finite disjoint union of exact-rank prime classes, and every labelled
+ladder slot has at most one candidate.
+\end{proposition}
+
+\begin{proof}
+If $\theta=q$ is a prime atom, the prime-ladder dichotomy gives
+$E_n(q)=T_n(q)$, and $q$ belongs to the unique class
+$\Pi_\alpha(d(q))$ in $P_{T_n(q)}(n)$. Conversely every prime in $P_J(n)$
+has $(E_n,T_n)=(J,J)$.
+
+Suppose $\theta=q^e$ is a ladder atom. The same dichotomy gives
+$E_n(\theta)=\{q\}$ whenever the essential support is nonempty. Hence its
+essential coordinate determines its underlying prime, so $q=p$. The
+full-exponent equation
+$\nu_p(d(p^e))=\nu_p(n)=a$ and
+Proposition~\ref{prop:prime-power-ladders} now leave only the displayed
+candidate. For $p=2$, the atomic ladder levels are $4$ of rank $6$ and
+$2^e$ of rank $3\cdot2^{e-2}$ for $e\ge4$. For $p=5$, the rank is $5^e$,
+and $e=1$ is a prime atom. For $p\notin\{2,5\}$, one has
+$p\nmid z_p$ and
+$\alpha(p^e)=p^{e-h_p}z_p$ at atomic ladder levels, so $e=h_p+a$.
+The remaining conditions $d(\theta)\mid n$ and $T_n(\theta)=J$ are exactly
+the conditions for membership in $\mathcal A_{\{p\},J}(n)$.
+
+Finally, each $\Pi_\alpha(d)$ is finite by
+Lemma~\ref{lem:primitive-prime-mobius-count}, and there are only finitely many
+divisors $d$ of $n$. This proves all finiteness and uniqueness assertions.
+\end{proof}

-\begin{theorem}[Fibotomic rank entropy]
+The Fibonacci polynomials were studied by Webb--Parberry
+\cite{WebbParberry1969FibonacciPolynomials}; Levy introduced the fibotomic
+polynomials and proved their irreducibility over $\mathbb Q$
+\cite{Levy2001FibonacciPolynomials}; and Byer--Dvorachek--Eckard--Harrington--
+Wise--Wong developed their later systematic theory
+\cite{CameronCountsLundMillerPiechnikWong2022Fibotomic}. We use only the
+definition and factorization identity recorded in the following lemma.
+
+\begin{lemma}[Fibotomic integer and exact-rank radical]
+\label{lem:fibotomic-integer-radical}
+Let $d\ge3$, let $\Psi_d(x)$ be the $d$th fibotomic polynomial, and put
+\[
+ \mathfrak F_d:=\prod_{r\mid d}F_r^{\mu(d/r)}.
+\]
+Then
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:fibotomic-integer-identity}
+ \mathfrak F_d=\Psi_d(1)\in\mathbb N,
+\end{equation}
+and
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:exact-rank-radical-divides-fibotomic}
+ \prod_{p\in\Pi_\alpha(d)}p\mid\mathfrak F_d.
+\end{equation}
+For $d=3,5$ the exact-rank radicals are respectively $2$ and $5$; for
+$d=6,12$ the exact-rank layer is empty, so the product in the second display
+is $1$.
+\end{lemma}
+
+\begin{proof}
+The polynomial factorization
+\[
+ F_d(x)=\prod_{r\mid d}\Psi_r(x)
+\]
+and M\"obius inversion in the multiplicative group of nonzero rational
+functions give
+\[
+ \Psi_d(x)=\prod_{r\mid d}F_r(x)^{\mu(d/r)}.
+\]
+Evaluation at $x=1$ proves
+$\mathfrak F_d=\Psi_d(1)$. The fibotomic polynomial has positive integral
+value at $1$, proving \eqref{eq:fibotomic-integer-identity} despite the
+negative exponents in the M\"obius expression.
+
+If $p\in\Pi_\alpha(d)$, then $p\mid F_d$ but $p\nmid F_r$ for every proper
+divisor $r$ of $d$. In the integral factorization
+$F_d=\prod_{r\mid d}\Psi_r(1)$, any divisibility
+$p\mid\Psi_r(1)$ with $r<d$ would imply $p\mid F_r$, because
+$\Psi_r(1)\mid F_r$. Hence $p\mid\Psi_d(1)=\mathfrak F_d$. Distinct
+exact-rank primes are coprime, which proves the radical divisibility without
+any appeal to cancellation in the M\"obius quotient. The small-rank claims
+follow from $\alpha(2)=3$, $\alpha(5)=5$, and the absence of exact-rank
+primes at ranks $6$ and $12$.
+\end{proof}

+\section{Fibonacci prime-power realization}
+\label{sec:prime-power-realization}
+
+The witness-cover classification is structural.  We now supply the
+Fibonacci-specific input that determines which prime powers can occur in its
+atomic families.  These formulas will be used explicitly in the upper bounds.
+
+\begin{proposition}[Classical prime-power rank lifting]
+\label{prop:prime-power-ladders}
+Let $p$ be prime, and put $z_p:=\alpha(p)$. For $p\ne2,5$, put
+$h_p:=\nu_p(F_{z_p})$. Then
+\[
+\alpha(2)=3,\qquad \alpha(4)=6,\qquad
+\alpha(2^e)=3\cdot2^{e-2}\quad(e\ge3),
+\]
+\[
+\alpha(5^e)=5^e\quad(e\ge1),
+\]
+and, for $p\ne2,5$,
+\[
+\alpha(p^e)=p^{\max\{e-h_p,0\}}z_p\quad(e\ge1).
+\]
+\end{proposition}
+
+\begin{proof}
+Wall's rank-divisibility theorem gives
+\[
+p\mid F_r\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad z_p\mid r
+\]
+\cite{Wall1960FibonacciModm}. For $p\ne2,5$, the classical congruence
+\[
+F_{p-(5/p)}\equiv0\pmod p
+\]
+gives $z_p\mid p-(5/p)$, so $p\nmid z_p$. Lengyel's valuation formula
+\cite[Theorems~1 and~2]{Lengyel1995OrderFibonacciLucas}, in the treatment of
+Medina--Rowland \cite{MedinaRowland2015PRegularity}, states that when
+$z_p\mid r$,
+\[
+\nu_p(F_r)=\nu_p(F_{z_p})+\nu_p(r).
+\]
+Writing $r=z_pu$ yields
+$\nu_p(F_{z_pu})=h_p+\nu_p(u)$. Thus $p^e\mid F_{z_pu}$ if and only if
+$\nu_p(u)\ge e-h_p$, and the least admissible $u$ is
+$p^{\max\{e-h_p,0\}}$.
+
+For the exceptional primes, the same valuation formulas specialize to
+\[
+\nu_5(F_r)=\nu_5(r),
+\qquad
+\nu_2(F_r)=
+\begin{cases}
+0, & 3\nmid r,\\
+1, & r\equiv3\pmod 6,\\
+3, & r\equiv6\pmod {12},\\
+\nu_2(r)+2, & 12\mid r.
+\end{cases}
+\]
+The least index divisible by $5^e$ is $5^e$. For $2$, the least indices
+with valuation at least $1$, $2$, and $3$ are $3$, $6$, and $6$; for
+$e\ge4$ the least admissible multiple of $12$ is $3\cdot2^{e-2}$.
+\end{proof}
+
+\begin{corollary}[Atomic prime-power classification]
+\label{cor:atomic-classification}
+The atomic prime powers are exactly the following:
+\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
+\item $2\in\Atom(3)$, $4\in\Atom(6)$, and
+$2^e\in\Atom(3\cdot2^{e-2})$ for every $e\ge4$; the power $8$ is not
+atomic.
+\item $5^e\in\Atom(5^e)$ for every $e\ge1$.
+\item If $p\ne2,5$, $z_p=\alpha(p)$, and
+$h_p=\nu_p(F_{z_p})$, then $p\in\Atom(z_p)$ and
+$p^e\in\Atom(p^{e-h_p}z_p)$ for every $e>h_p$; no power $p^e$ with
+$1<e\le h_p$ is atomic.
+\end{enumerate}
+Consequently every atom is either a prime atom or a ladder atom $p^e$ with
+$e>1$. Every ladder step changes only the $p$-adic coordinate of its
+apparition index when it is lowered to $p^{e-1}$.
+\end{corollary}
+
+\begin{proof}
+Apply Proposition~\ref{prop:prime-power-ladders}. For $p=2$, the ranks are
+$3,6,6,12,24,\ldots$ on $2,4,8,16,32,\ldots$. For $p=5$, every step is
+atomic. If $p\ne2,5$, the rank remains $z_p$ for $1\le e\le h_p$ and then
+gains one factor of $p$ at each further level. The last assertion follows
+from the same formulas.
+\end{proof}
+
+\begin{lemma}[Prime-ladder dichotomy]
+\label{thm:primitive-ladder-dichotomy}
+Let $\theta=p^e\in\Atom(d)$ and suppose $d\mid n$. If $e=1$, then
+\[
+E_n(\theta)=T_n(\theta).
+\]
+If $e>1$, then $E_n(\theta)$ is either empty or the singleton $\{p\}$.
+In particular, no Fibonacci atom has
+\[
+1<\#E_n(\theta)<\#T_n(\theta).
+\]
+\end{lemma}
+
+\begin{proof}
+If $e=1$, then $d^-(\theta)=\alpha(1)=1$, so every coordinate in
+$T_n(\theta)$ is lost after lowering. Assume $e>1$. By
+Corollary~\ref{cor:atomic-classification}, $\theta$ is a ladder atom.
+Proposition~\ref{prop:prime-power-ladders} shows that $d(\theta)$ and
+$d^-(\theta)$ differ only in their $p$-adic coordinate. Therefore the only
+full coordinate that can be lost is $p$ itself, and the result follows.
+\end{proof}
+
+For nonempty $J\subseteq\mathcal P(n)$, define the prime window
+\[
+P_J(n):=\coprod_{\substack{d\mid n\\T_n(d)=J}}\Pi_\alpha(d),
+\]
+where $T_n(d)=\{\ell\in\mathcal P(n):
+\nu_\ell(d)=\nu_\ell(n)\}$.  A prime in $P_J(n)$ is identified with its
+prime atom.
+
+\begin{proposition}[Atomic families and unique ladder slots]
+\label{prop:atomic-family-ladder-slots}
+Let $n\ge3$ and let $\varnothing\ne I\subseteq J\subseteq\mathcal P(n)$.
+Then every atom in $\mathcal A_{I,J}(n)$ is either in the prime window
+$P_J(n)$, which occurs only when $I=J$, or in a ladder family with
+$I=\{p\}$ for a prime coordinate $p\in J$.  Each such ladder family contains
+at most one atom.
+
+More precisely, put $a=\nu_p(n)$.  Its only possible ladder atom is
+\[
+\lambda_p(n)=
+\begin{cases}
+4, & p=2,\ a=1,\\
+2^{a+2}, & p=2,\ a\ge2,\\
+5^a, & p=5,\ a\ge2,\\
+p^{h_p+a}, & p\notin\{2,5\},
+\end{cases}
+\]
+with no candidate for $p=5$, $a=1$.  The candidate belongs to
+$\mathcal A_{\{p\},J}(n)$ exactly when
+$d(\lambda_p(n))\mid n$ and $T_n(\lambda_p(n))=J$.
+Consequently every atomic family is finite, every nonsingleton atomic family
+is a finite disjoint union of exact-rank prime classes, and every labelled
+ladder slot has at most one candidate.
+\end{proposition}
+
+\begin{proof}
+If $\theta=q$ is a prime atom, the prime-ladder dichotomy gives
+$E_n(q)=T_n(q)$, and $q$ belongs to the unique class
+$\Pi_\alpha(d(q))$ in $P_{T_n(q)}(n)$. Conversely every prime in $P_J(n)$
+has $(E_n,T_n)=(J,J)$.
+
+Suppose $\theta=q^e$ is a ladder atom. The same dichotomy gives
+$E_n(\theta)=\{q\}$ whenever the essential support is nonempty. Hence its
+essential coordinate determines its underlying prime, so $q=p$. The
+full-exponent equation
+$\nu_p(d(p^e))=\nu_p(n)=a$ and
+Proposition~\ref{prop:prime-power-ladders} now leave only the displayed
+candidate. For $p=2$, the atomic ladder levels are $4$ of rank $6$ and
+$2^e$ of rank $3\cdot2^{e-2}$ for $e\ge4$. For $p=5$, the rank is $5^e$,
+and $e=1$ is a prime atom. For $p\notin\{2,5\}$, one has
+$p\nmid z_p$ and
+$\alpha(p^e)=p^{e-h_p}z_p$ at atomic ladder levels, so $e=h_p+a$.
+The remaining conditions $d(\theta)\mid n$ and $T_n(\theta)=J$ are exactly
+the conditions for membership in $\mathcal A_{\{p\},J}(n)$.
+
+Finally, each $\Pi_\alpha(d)$ is finite by
+Lemma~\ref{lem:primitive-prime-mobius-count}, and there are only finitely many
+divisors $d$ of $n$. This proves all finiteness and uniqueness assertions.
+\end{proof}

-\begin{theorem}[Fibotomic rank entropy]
+The Fibonacci polynomials were studied by Webb--Parberry
+\cite{WebbParberry1969FibonacciPolynomials}; Levy introduced the fibotomic
+polynomials and proved their irreducibility over $\mathbb Q$
+\cite{Levy2001FibonacciPolynomials}; and Byer--Dvorachek--Eckard--Harrington--
+Wise--Wong developed their later systematic theory
+\cite{CameronCountsLundMillerPiechnikWong2022Fibotomic}. We use only the
+definition and factorization identity recorded in the following lemma.
+
+\begin{lemma}[Fibotomic integer and exact-rank radical]
+\label{lem:fibotomic-integer-radical}
+Let $d\ge3$, let $\Psi_d(x)$ be the $d$th fibotomic polynomial, and put
+\[

+\end{equation}

+\end{equation}

+\end{lemma}

+\begin{proof}
+The polynomial factorization
+\[

+\]

+\[

+\]
+Evaluation at $x=1$ proves
+$\mathfrak F_d=\Psi_d(1)$. The fibotomic polynomial has positive integral
+value at $1$, proving \eqref{eq:fibotomic-integer-identity} despite the
+negative exponents in the M\"obius expression.

+any appeal to cancellation in the M\"obius quotient. The small-rank claims

+primes at ranks $6$ and $12$.
+\end{proof}

+\begin{proposition}[Wagner comparison and lowered labels]
+\label{prop:wagner-comparison}
+Let $n\ge2$, and let $\Theta=\{p_1,\ldots,p_r\}$ be a set of distinct prime
+atoms with $d_i:=\alpha(p_i)\mid n$. Then $\Theta$ is an $n$-witness cover
+if and only if, after forgetting the order of the tuple
+$(d_1,\ldots,d_r)$,
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:wagner-minimal-multiplicative-cover}
+ \lcmop(d_1,\ldots,d_r)=n,
+ \qquad
+ \lcmop(d_1,\ldots,\widehat{d_i},\ldots,d_r)<n
+ \quad(1\le i\le r).
+\end{equation}
+Thus the prime-atom case is precisely the unordered form of Wagner's minimal
+multiplicative cover condition.
+
+For arbitrary pairwise coprime atoms
+$\Theta=\{\theta_1,\ldots,\theta_r\}$, the witness condition replaces the
+deletion in \eqref{eq:wagner-minimal-multiplicative-cover} by
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:lowered-label-multiplicative-cover}
+ \lcmop\bigl(d(\theta_1),\ldots,d^-(\theta_i),\ldots,
+ d(\theta_r)\bigr)<n
+ \quad(1\le i\le r).
+\end{equation}
+In particular, ladder atoms supply the genuinely additional lowered-label
+case: their label is lowered to $d^-(\theta_i)$ rather than deleted.
+\end{proposition}
+
+\begin{proof}
+For a prime atom $p_i$, one has $d^-(p_i)=\alpha(1)=1$. Hence replacing
+$d_i$ by $d^-(p_i)$ in an lcm is identical to omitting $d_i$. Lemma~
+\ref{thm:minimal-generators} and Lemma~\ref{lem:coordinate-lowering-test}
+then identify the witness-cover conditions with
+\eqref{eq:wagner-minimal-multiplicative-cover}. Since the labels form a
+minimal cover, no repeated label can occur; forgetting tuple order therefore
+produces the corresponding unordered cover without a multiplicity ambiguity.
+
+For arbitrary atoms, the same two lemmas say exactly that the full apparition
+lcm is $n$ and that lowering each atom produces
+\eqref{eq:lowered-label-multiplicative-cover}. The final assertion is the
+distinction between $d^-(p)=1$ for prime atoms and the nontrivial lower rank
+of a ladder atom.
+\end{proof}
+
+Wagner's condition and its set-theoretic predecessor supply the classical
+cover skeleton. The Fibonacci-specific content below is the arithmetic
+realization of its labels by exact-rank primes, the lowered-label refinement
+forced by prime-power ladders, and the unique correspondence with
+$\mathcal M_n$. The canonical squarefree slice and its exact weighted count
+in Section~\ref{sec:rank-pure} are further arithmetic consequences of that
+realization.

+\section{Fibonacci prime-power realization}
+\label{sec:prime-power-realization}
+
+The witness-cover classification is structural.  We now supply the
+Fibonacci-specific input that determines which prime powers can occur in its
+atomic families.  These formulas will be used explicitly in the upper bounds.
+
+\begin{proposition}[Classical prime-power rank lifting]
+\label{prop:prime-power-ladders}
+Let $p$ be prime, and put $z_p:=\alpha(p)$. For $p\ne2,5$, put
+$h_p:=\nu_p(F_{z_p})$. Then
+\[
+\alpha(2)=3,\qquad \alpha(4)=6,\qquad
+\alpha(2^e)=3\cdot2^{e-2}\quad(e\ge3),
+\]
+\[
+\alpha(5^e)=5^e\quad(e\ge1),
+\]
+and, for $p\ne2,5$,
+\[
+\alpha(p^e)=p^{\max\{e-h_p,0\}}z_p\quad(e\ge1).
+\]
+\end{proposition}
+
+\begin{proof}
+Wall's rank-divisibility theorem gives
+\[
+p\mid F_r\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad z_p\mid r
+\]
+\cite{Wall1960FibonacciModm}. For $p\ne2,5$, the classical congruence
+\[
+F_{p-(5/p)}\equiv0\pmod p
+\]
+gives $z_p\mid p-(5/p)$, so $p\nmid z_p$. Lengyel's valuation formula
+\cite[Theorems~1 and~2]{Lengyel1995OrderFibonacciLucas}, in the treatment of
+Medina--Rowland \cite{MedinaRowland2015PRegularity}, states that when
+$z_p\mid r$,
+\[
+\nu_p(F_r)=\nu_p(F_{z_p})+\nu_p(r).
+\]
+Writing $r=z_pu$ yields
+$\nu_p(F_{z_pu})=h_p+\nu_p(u)$. Thus $p^e\mid F_{z_pu}$ if and only if
+$\nu_p(u)\ge e-h_p$, and the least admissible $u$ is
+$p^{\max\{e-h_p,0\}}$.
+
+For the exceptional primes, the same valuation formulas specialize to
+\[
+\nu_5(F_r)=\nu_5(r),
+\qquad
+\nu_2(F_r)=
+\begin{cases}
+0, & 3\nmid r,\\
+1, & r\equiv3\pmod 6,\\
+3, & r\equiv6\pmod {12},\\
+\nu_2(r)+2, & 12\mid r.
+\end{cases}
+\]
+The least index divisible by $5^e$ is $5^e$. For $2$, the least indices
+with valuation at least $1$, $2$, and $3$ are $3$, $6$, and $6$; for
+$e\ge4$ the least admissible multiple of $12$ is $3\cdot2^{e-2}$.
+\end{proof}
+
+\begin{corollary}[Atomic prime-power classification]
+\label{cor:atomic-classification}
+The atomic prime powers are exactly the following:
+\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
+\item $2\in\Atom(3)$, $4\in\Atom(6)$, and
+$2^e\in\Atom(3\cdot2^{e-2})$ for every $e\ge4$; the power $8$ is not
+atomic.
+\item $5^e\in\Atom(5^e)$ for every $e\ge1$.
+\item If $p\ne2,5$, $z_p=\alpha(p)$, and
+$h_p=\nu_p(F_{z_p})$, then $p\in\Atom(z_p)$ and
+$p^e\in\Atom(p^{e-h_p}z_p)$ for every $e>h_p$; no power $p^e$ with
+$1<e\le h_p$ is atomic.
+\end{enumerate}
+Consequently every atom is either a prime atom or a ladder atom $p^e$ with
+$e>1$. Every ladder step changes only the $p$-adic coordinate of its
+apparition index when it is lowered to $p^{e-1}$.
+\end{corollary}
+
+\begin{proof}
+Apply Proposition~\ref{prop:prime-power-ladders}. For $p=2$, the ranks are
+$3,6,6,12,24,\ldots$ on $2,4,8,16,32,\ldots$. For $p=5$, every step is
+atomic. If $p\ne2,5$, the rank remains $z_p$ for $1\le e\le h_p$ and then
+gains one factor of $p$ at each further level. The last assertion follows
+from the same formulas.
+\end{proof}
+
+\begin{lemma}[Prime-ladder dichotomy]
+\label{thm:primitive-ladder-dichotomy}
+Let $\theta=p^e\in\Atom(d)$ and suppose $d\mid n$. If $e=1$, then
+\[
+E_n(\theta)=T_n(\theta).
+\]
+If $e>1$, then $E_n(\theta)$ is either empty or the singleton $\{p\}$.
+In particular, no Fibonacci atom has
+\[
+1<\#E_n(\theta)<\#T_n(\theta).
+\]
+\end{lemma}
+
+\begin{proof}
+If $e=1$, then $d^-(\theta)=\alpha(1)=1$, so every coordinate in
+$T_n(\theta)$ is lost after lowering. Assume $e>1$. By
+Corollary~\ref{cor:atomic-classification}, $\theta$ is a ladder atom.
+Proposition~\ref{prop:prime-power-ladders} shows that $d(\theta)$ and
+$d^-(\theta)$ differ only in their $p$-adic coordinate. Therefore the only
+full coordinate that can be lost is $p$ itself, and the result follows.
+\end{proof}
+
+For nonempty $J\subseteq\mathcal P(n)$, define the prime window
+\[
+P_J(n):=\coprod_{\substack{d\mid n\\T_n(d)=J}}\Pi_\alpha(d),
+\]
+where $T_n(d)=\{\ell\in\mathcal P(n):
+\nu_\ell(d)=\nu_\ell(n)\}$.  A prime in $P_J(n)$ is identified with its
+prime atom.
+
+\begin{proposition}[Atomic families and unique ladder slots]
+\label{prop:atomic-family-ladder-slots}
+Let $n\ge3$ and let $\varnothing\ne I\subseteq J\subseteq\mathcal P(n)$.
+Then every atom in $\mathcal A_{I,J}(n)$ is either in the prime window
+$P_J(n)$, which occurs only when $I=J$, or in a ladder family with
+$I=\{p\}$ for a prime coordinate $p\in J$.  Each such ladder family contains
+at most one atom.
+
+More precisely, put $a=\nu_p(n)$.  Its only possible ladder atom is
+\[
+\lambda_p(n)=
+\begin{cases}
+4, & p=2,\ a=1,\\
+2^{a+2}, & p=2,\ a\ge2,\\
+5^a, & p=5,\ a\ge2,\\
+p^{h_p+a}, & p\notin\{2,5\},
+\end{cases}
+\]
+with no candidate for $p=5$, $a=1$.  The candidate belongs to
+$\mathcal A_{\{p\},J}(n)$ exactly when
+$d(\lambda_p(n))\mid n$ and $T_n(\lambda_p(n))=J$.
+Consequently every atomic family is finite, every nonsingleton atomic family
+is a finite disjoint union of exact-rank prime classes, and every labelled
+ladder slot has at most one candidate.
+\end{proposition}
+
+\begin{proof}
+If $\theta=q$ is a prime atom, the prime-ladder dichotomy gives
+$E_n(q)=T_n(q)$, and $q$ belongs to the unique class
+$\Pi_\alpha(d(q))$ in $P_{T_n(q)}(n)$. Conversely every prime in $P_J(n)$
+has $(E_n,T_n)=(J,J)$.
+
+Suppose $\theta=q^e$ is a ladder atom. The same dichotomy gives
+$E_n(\theta)=\{q\}$ whenever the essential support is nonempty. Hence its
+essential coordinate determines its underlying prime, so $q=p$. The
+full-exponent equation
+$\nu_p(d(p^e))=\nu_p(n)=a$ and
+Proposition~\ref{prop:prime-power-ladders} now leave only the displayed
+candidate. For $p=2$, the atomic ladder levels are $4$ of rank $6$ and
+$2^e$ of rank $3\cdot2^{e-2}$ for $e\ge4$. For $p=5$, the rank is $5^e$,
+and $e=1$ is a prime atom. For $p\notin\{2,5\}$, one has
+$p\nmid z_p$ and
+$\alpha(p^e)=p^{e-h_p}z_p$ at atomic ladder levels, so $e=h_p+a$.
+The remaining conditions $d(\theta)\mid n$ and $T_n(\theta)=J$ are exactly
+the conditions for membership in $\mathcal A_{\{p\},J}(n)$.
+
+Finally, each $\Pi_\alpha(d)$ is finite by
+Lemma~\ref{lem:primitive-prime-mobius-count}, and there are only finitely many
+divisors $d$ of $n$. This proves all finiteness and uniqueness assertions.
+\end{proof}

-\begin{theorem}[Fibotomic rank entropy]
+The Fibonacci polynomials were studied by Webb--Parberry
+\cite{WebbParberry1969FibonacciPolynomials}; Levy introduced the fibotomic
+polynomials and proved their irreducibility over $\mathbb Q$
+\cite{Levy2001FibonacciPolynomials}; and Byer--Dvorachek--Eckard--Harrington--
+Wise--Wong developed their later systematic theory
+\cite{CameronCountsLundMillerPiechnikWong2022Fibotomic}. We use only the
+definition and factorization identity recorded in the following lemma.
+
+\begin{lemma}[Fibotomic integer and exact-rank radical]
+\label{lem:fibotomic-integer-radical}
+Let $d\ge3$, let $\Psi_d(x)$ be the $d$th fibotomic polynomial, and put
+\[
+ \mathfrak F_d:=\prod_{r\mid d}F_r^{\mu(d/r)}.
+\]
+Then
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:fibotomic-integer-identity}
+ \mathfrak F_d=\Psi_d(1)\in\mathbb N,
+\end{equation}
+and
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:exact-rank-radical-divides-fibotomic}
+ \prod_{p\in\Pi_\alpha(d)}p\mid\mathfrak F_d.
+\end{equation}
+For $d=3,5$ the exact-rank radicals are respectively $2$ and $5$; for
+$d=6,12$ the exact-rank layer is empty, so the product in the second display
+is $1$.
+\end{lemma}
+
+\begin{proof}
+The polynomial factorization
+\[
+ F_d(x)=\prod_{r\mid d}\Psi_r(x)
+\]
+and M\"obius inversion in the multiplicative group of nonzero rational
+functions give
+\[
+ \Psi_d(x)=\prod_{r\mid d}F_r(x)^{\mu(d/r)}.
+\]
+Evaluation at $x=1$ proves
+$\mathfrak F_d=\Psi_d(1)$. The fibotomic polynomial has positive integral
+value at $1$, proving \eqref{eq:fibotomic-integer-identity} despite the
+negative exponents in the M\"obius expression.
+
+If $p\in\Pi_\alpha(d)$, then $p\mid F_d$ but $p\nmid F_r$ for every proper
+divisor $r$ of $d$. In the integral factorization
+$F_d=\prod_{r\mid d}\Psi_r(1)$, any divisibility
+$p\mid\Psi_r(1)$ with $r<d$ would imply $p\mid F_r$, because
+$\Psi_r(1)\mid F_r$. Hence $p\mid\Psi_d(1)=\mathfrak F_d$. Distinct
+exact-rank primes are coprime, which proves the radical divisibility without
+any appeal to cancellation in the M\"obius quotient. The small-rank claims
+follow from $\alpha(2)=3$, $\alpha(5)=5$, and the absence of exact-rank
+primes at ranks $6$ and $12$.
+\end{proof}
+

-\begin{theorem}\label{thm:witness-classification}

+\begin{proposition}[Wagner comparison and lowered labels]
+\label{prop:wagner-comparison}
+Let $n\ge2$, and let $\Theta=\{p_1,\ldots,p_r\}$ be a set of distinct prime
+atoms with $d_i:=\alpha(p_i)\mid n$. Then $\Theta$ is an $n$-witness cover
+if and only if, after forgetting the order of the tuple
+$(d_1,\ldots,d_r)$,
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:wagner-minimal-multiplicative-cover}
+ \lcmop(d_1,\ldots,d_r)=n,
+ \qquad
+ \lcmop(d_1,\ldots,\widehat{d_i},\ldots,d_r)<n
+ \quad(1\le i\le r).
+\end{equation}
+Thus the prime-atom case is precisely the unordered form of Wagner's minimal
+multiplicative cover condition.
+
+For arbitrary pairwise coprime atoms
+$\Theta=\{\theta_1,\ldots,\theta_r\}$, the witness condition replaces the
+deletion in \eqref{eq:wagner-minimal-multiplicative-cover} by
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:lowered-label-multiplicative-cover}
+ \lcmop\bigl(d(\theta_1),\ldots,d^-(\theta_i),\ldots,
+ d(\theta_r)\bigr)<n
+ \quad(1\le i\le r).
+\end{equation}
+In particular, ladder atoms supply the genuinely additional lowered-label
+case: their label is lowered to $d^-(\theta_i)$ rather than deleted.
+\end{proposition}
+
+\begin{proof}
+For a prime atom $p_i$, one has $d^-(p_i)=\alpha(1)=1$. Hence replacing
+$d_i$ by $d^-(p_i)$ in an lcm is identical to omitting $d_i$. Lemma~
+\ref{thm:minimal-generators} and Lemma~\ref{lem:coordinate-lowering-test}
+then identify the witness-cover conditions with
+\eqref{eq:wagner-minimal-multiplicative-cover}. Since the labels form a
+minimal cover, no repeated label can occur; forgetting tuple order therefore
+produces the corresponding unordered cover without a multiplicity ambiguity.
+
+For arbitrary atoms, the same two lemmas say exactly that the full apparition
+lcm is $n$ and that lowering each atom produces
+\eqref{eq:lowered-label-multiplicative-cover}. The final assertion is the
+distinction between $d^-(p)=1$ for prime atoms and the nontrivial lower rank
+of a ladder atom.
+\end{proof}
+
+Wagner's condition and its set-theoretic predecessor supply the classical
+cover skeleton. The Fibonacci-specific content below is the arithmetic
+realization of its labels by exact-rank primes, the lowered-label refinement
+forced by prime-power ladders, and the unique correspondence with
+$\mathcal M_n$. The canonical squarefree slice and its exact weighted count
+in Section~\ref{sec:rank-pure} are further arithmetic consequences of that
+realization.
+

+\section{Fibonacci prime-power realization}
+\label{sec:prime-power-realization}
+
+The witness-cover classification is structural.  We now supply the
+Fibonacci-specific input that determines which prime powers can occur in its
+atomic families.  These formulas will be used explicitly in the upper bounds.
+
+\begin{proposition}[Classical prime-power rank lifting]
+\label{prop:prime-power-ladders}
+Let $p$ be prime, and put $z_p:=\alpha(p)$. For $p\ne2,5$, put
+$h_p:=\nu_p(F_{z_p})$. Then
+\[
+\alpha(2)=3,\qquad \alpha(4)=6,\qquad
+\alpha(2^e)=3\cdot2^{e-2}\quad(e\ge3),
+\]
+\[
+\alpha(5^e)=5^e\quad(e\ge1),
+\]
+and, for $p\ne2,5$,
+\[
+\alpha(p^e)=p^{\max\{e-h_p,0\}}z_p\quad(e\ge1).
+\]
+\end{proposition}
+
+\begin{proof}
+Wall's rank-divisibility theorem gives
+\[
+p\mid F_r\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad z_p\mid r
+\]
+\cite{Wall1960FibonacciModm}. For $p\ne2,5$, the classical congruence
+\[
+F_{p-(5/p)}\equiv0\pmod p
+\]
+gives $z_p\mid p-(5/p)$, so $p\nmid z_p$. Lengyel's valuation formula
+\cite[Theorems~1 and~2]{Lengyel1995OrderFibonacciLucas}, in the treatment of
+Medina--Rowland \cite{MedinaRowland2015PRegularity}, states that when
+$z_p\mid r$,
+\[
+\nu_p(F_r)=\nu_p(F_{z_p})+\nu_p(r).
+\]
+Writing $r=z_pu$ yields
+$\nu_p(F_{z_pu})=h_p+\nu_p(u)$. Thus $p^e\mid F_{z_pu}$ if and only if
+$\nu_p(u)\ge e-h_p$, and the least admissible $u$ is
+$p^{\max\{e-h_p,0\}}$.
+
+For the exceptional primes, the same valuation formulas specialize to
+\[
+\nu_5(F_r)=\nu_5(r),
+\qquad
+\nu_2(F_r)=
+\begin{cases}
+0, & 3\nmid r,\\
+1, & r\equiv3\pmod 6,\\
+3, & r\equiv6\pmod {12},\\
+\nu_2(r)+2, & 12\mid r.
+\end{cases}
+\]
+The least index divisible by $5^e$ is $5^e$. For $2$, the least indices
+with valuation at least $1$, $2$, and $3$ are $3$, $6$, and $6$; for
+$e\ge4$ the least admissible multiple of $12$ is $3\cdot2^{e-2}$.
+\end{proof}
+
+\begin{corollary}[Atomic prime-power classification]
+\label{cor:atomic-classification}
+The atomic prime powers are exactly the following:
+\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
+\item $2\in\Atom(3)$, $4\in\Atom(6)$, and
+$2^e\in\Atom(3\cdot2^{e-2})$ for every $e\ge4$; the power $8$ is not
+atomic.
+\item $5^e\in\Atom(5^e)$ for every $e\ge1$.
+\item If $p\ne2,5$, $z_p=\alpha(p)$, and
+$h_p=\nu_p(F_{z_p})$, then $p\in\Atom(z_p)$ and
+$p^e\in\Atom(p^{e-h_p}z_p)$ for every $e>h_p$; no power $p^e$ with
+$1<e\le h_p$ is atomic.
+\end{enumerate}
+Consequently every atom is either a prime atom or a ladder atom $p^e$ with
+$e>1$. Every ladder step changes only the $p$-adic coordinate of its
+apparition index when it is lowered to $p^{e-1}$.
+\end{corollary}
+
+\begin{proof}
+Apply Proposition~\ref{prop:prime-power-ladders}. For $p=2$, the ranks are
+$3,6,6,12,24,\ldots$ on $2,4,8,16,32,\ldots$. For $p=5$, every step is
+atomic. If $p\ne2,5$, the rank remains $z_p$ for $1\le e\le h_p$ and then
+gains one factor of $p$ at each further level. The last assertion follows
+from the same formulas.
+\end{proof}
+
+\begin{lemma}[Prime-ladder dichotomy]
+\label{thm:primitive-ladder-dichotomy}
+Let $\theta=p^e\in\Atom(d)$ and suppose $d\mid n$. If $e=1$, then
+\[
+E_n(\theta)=T_n(\theta).
+\]
+If $e>1$, then $E_n(\theta)$ is either empty or the singleton $\{p\}$.
+In particular, no Fibonacci atom has
+\[
+1<\#E_n(\theta)<\#T_n(\theta).
+\]
+\end{lemma}
+
+\begin{proof}
+If $e=1$, then $d^-(\theta)=\alpha(1)=1$, so every coordinate in
+$T_n(\theta)$ is lost after lowering. Assume $e>1$. By
+Corollary~\ref{cor:atomic-classification}, $\theta$ is a ladder atom.
+Proposition~\ref{prop:prime-power-ladders} shows that $d(\theta)$ and
+$d^-(\theta)$ differ only in their $p$-adic coordinate. Therefore the only
+full coordinate that can be lost is $p$ itself, and the result follows.
+\end{proof}
+
+For nonempty $J\subseteq\mathcal P(n)$, define the prime window
+\[
+P_J(n):=\coprod_{\substack{d\mid n\\T_n(d)=J}}\Pi_\alpha(d),
+\]
+where $T_n(d)=\{\ell\in\mathcal P(n):
+\nu_\ell(d)=\nu_\ell(n)\}$.  A prime in $P_J(n)$ is identified with its
+prime atom.
+
+\begin{proposition}[Atomic families and unique ladder slots]
+\label{prop:atomic-family-ladder-slots}
+Let $n\ge3$ and let $\varnothing\ne I\subseteq J\subseteq\mathcal P(n)$.
+Then every atom in $\mathcal A_{I,J}(n)$ is either in the prime window
+$P_J(n)$, which occurs only when $I=J$, or in a ladder family with
+$I=\{p\}$ for a prime coordinate $p\in J$.  Each such ladder family contains
+at most one atom.
+
+More precisely, put $a=\nu_p(n)$.  Its only possible ladder atom is
+\[
+\lambda_p(n)=
+\begin{cases}
+4, & p=2,\ a=1,\\
+2^{a+2}, & p=2,\ a\ge2,\\
+5^a, & p=5,\ a\ge2,\\
+p^{h_p+a}, & p\notin\{2,5\},
+\end{cases}
+\]
+with no candidate for $p=5$, $a=1$.  The candidate belongs to
+$\mathcal A_{\{p\},J}(n)$ exactly when
+$d(\lambda_p(n))\mid n$ and $T_n(\lambda_p(n))=J$.
+Consequently every atomic family is finite, every nonsingleton atomic family
+is a finite disjoint union of exact-rank prime classes, and every labelled
+ladder slot has at most one candidate.
+\end{proposition}
+
+\begin{proof}
+If $\theta=q$ is a prime atom, the prime-ladder dichotomy gives
+$E_n(q)=T_n(q)$, and $q$ belongs to the unique class
+$\Pi_\alpha(d(q))$ in $P_{T_n(q)}(n)$. Conversely every prime in $P_J(n)$
+has $(E_n,T_n)=(J,J)$.
+
+Suppose $\theta=q^e$ is a ladder atom. The same dichotomy gives
+$E_n(\theta)=\{q\}$ whenever the essential support is nonempty. Hence its
+essential coordinate determines its underlying prime, so $q=p$. The
+full-exponent equation
+$\nu_p(d(p^e))=\nu_p(n)=a$ and
+Proposition~\ref{prop:prime-power-ladders} now leave only the displayed
+candidate. For $p=2$, the atomic ladder levels are $4$ of rank $6$ and
+$2^e$ of rank $3\cdot2^{e-2}$ for $e\ge4$. For $p=5$, the rank is $5^e$,
+and $e=1$ is a prime atom. For $p\notin\{2,5\}$, one has
+$p\nmid z_p$ and
+$\alpha(p^e)=p^{e-h_p}z_p$ at atomic ladder levels, so $e=h_p+a$.
+The remaining conditions $d(\theta)\mid n$ and $T_n(\theta)=J$ are exactly
+the conditions for membership in $\mathcal A_{\{p\},J}(n)$.
+
+Finally, each $\Pi_\alpha(d)$ is finite by
+Lemma~\ref{lem:primitive-prime-mobius-count}, and there are only finitely many
+divisors $d$ of $n$. This proves all finiteness and uniqueness assertions.
+\end{proof}

-\begin{theorem}[Fibotomic rank entropy]
+The Fibonacci polynomials were studied by Webb--Parberry
+\cite{WebbParberry1969FibonacciPolynomials}; Levy introduced the fibotomic
+polynomials and proved their irreducibility over $\mathbb Q$
+\cite{Levy2001FibonacciPolynomials}; and Byer--Dvorachek--Eckard--Harrington--
+Wise--Wong developed their later systematic theory
+\cite{CameronCountsLundMillerPiechnikWong2022Fibotomic}. We use only the
+definition and factorization identity recorded in the following lemma.
+
+\begin{lemma}[Fibotomic integer and exact-rank radical]
+\label{lem:fibotomic-integer-radical}
+Let $d\ge3$, let $\Psi_d(x)$ be the $d$th fibotomic polynomial, and put
+\[
+ \mathfrak F_d:=\prod_{r\mid d}F_r^{\mu(d/r)}.
+\]
+Then
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:fibotomic-integer-identity}
+ \mathfrak F_d=\Psi_d(1)\in\mathbb N,
+\end{equation}
+and
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:exact-rank-radical-divides-fibotomic}
+ \prod_{p\in\Pi_\alpha(d)}p\mid\mathfrak F_d.
+\end{equation}
+For $d=3,5$ the exact-rank radicals are respectively $2$ and $5$; for
+$d=6,12$ the exact-rank layer is empty, so the product in the second display
+is $1$.
+\end{lemma}
+
+\begin{proof}
+The polynomial factorization
+\[
+ F_d(x)=\prod_{r\mid d}\Psi_r(x)
+\]
+and M\"obius inversion in the multiplicative group of nonzero rational
+functions give
+\[
+ \Psi_d(x)=\prod_{r\mid d}F_r(x)^{\mu(d/r)}.
+\]
+Evaluation at $x=1$ proves
+$\mathfrak F_d=\Psi_d(1)$. The fibotomic polynomial has positive integral
+value at $1$, proving \eqref{eq:fibotomic-integer-identity} despite the
+negative exponents in the M\"obius expression.
+
+If $p\in\Pi_\alpha(d)$, then $p\mid F_d$ but $p\nmid F_r$ for every proper
+divisor $r$ of $d$. In the integral factorization
+$F_d=\prod_{r\mid d}\Psi_r(1)$, any divisibility
+$p\mid\Psi_r(1)$ with $r<d$ would imply $p\mid F_r$, because
+$\Psi_r(1)\mid F_r$. Hence $p\mid\Psi_d(1)=\mathfrak F_d$. Distinct
+exact-rank primes are coprime, which proves the radical divisibility without
+any appeal to cancellation in the M\"obius quotient. The small-rank claims
+follow from $\alpha(2)=3$, $\alpha(5)=5$, and the absence of exact-rank
+primes at ranks $6$ and $12$.
+\end{proof}
+

+\begin{proposition}[Wagner comparison and lowered labels]
+\label{prop:wagner-comparison}
+Let $n\ge2$, and let $\Theta=\{p_1,\ldots,p_r\}$ be a set of distinct prime
+atoms with $d_i:=\alpha(p_i)\mid n$. Then $\Theta$ is an $n$-witness cover
+if and only if, after forgetting the order of the tuple
+$(d_1,\ldots,d_r)$,
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:wagner-minimal-multiplicative-cover}
+ \lcmop(d_1,\ldots,d_r)=n,
+ \qquad
+ \lcmop(d_1,\ldots,\widehat{d_i},\ldots,d_r)<n
+ \quad(1\le i\le r).
+\end{equation}
+Thus the prime-atom case is precisely the unordered form of Wagner's minimal
+multiplicative cover condition.
+
+For arbitrary pairwise coprime atoms
+$\Theta=\{\theta_1,\ldots,\theta_r\}$, the witness condition replaces the
+deletion in \eqref{eq:wagner-minimal-multiplicative-cover} by
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:lowered-label-multiplicative-cover}
+ \lcmop\bigl(d(\theta_1),\ldots,d^-(\theta_i),\ldots,
+ d(\theta_r)\bigr)<n
+ \quad(1\le i\le r).
+\end{equation}
+In particular, ladder atoms supply the genuinely additional lowered-label
+case: their label is lowered to $d^-(\theta_i)$ rather than deleted.
+\end{proposition}
+
+\begin{proof}
+For a prime atom $p_i$, one has $d^-(p_i)=\alpha(1)=1$. Hence replacing
+$d_i$ by $d^-(p_i)$ in an lcm is identical to omitting $d_i$. Lemma~
+\ref{thm:minimal-generators} and Lemma~\ref{lem:coordinate-lowering-test}
+then identify the witness-cover conditions with
+\eqref{eq:wagner-minimal-multiplicative-cover}. Since the labels form a
+minimal cover, no repeated label can occur; forgetting tuple order therefore
+produces the corresponding unordered cover without a multiplicity ambiguity.
+
+For arbitrary atoms, the same two lemmas say exactly that the full apparition
+lcm is $n$ and that lowering each atom produces
+\eqref{eq:lowered-label-multiplicative-cover}. The final assertion is the
+distinction between $d^-(p)=1$ for prime atoms and the nontrivial lower rank
+of a ladder atom.
+\end{proof}
+
+Wagner's condition and its set-theoretic predecessor supply the classical
+cover skeleton. The Fibonacci-specific content below is the arithmetic
+realization of its labels by exact-rank primes, the lowered-label refinement
+forced by prime-power ladders, and the unique correspondence with
+$\mathcal M_n$. The canonical squarefree slice and its exact weighted count
+in Section~\ref{sec:rank-pure} are further arithmetic consequences of that
+realization.
